chienNous.jaugesTitre: The dogs that would suit you best
chienNous.invitationDuo: And what does your other half think? Take the quiz again together: you each answer separately, and you'll see where you disagree.
chienNous.noteFin: This quiz is a game: it gives you a lead, not a breeder's or a vet's opinion. Before you adopt, go and meet the dog and talk to people who know the breed.
chienNous.p_golden_d: The family dog if ever there was one: gentle, playful, patient, and happy with whatever you suggest. It learns fast, gets on with everyone, and needs you as much as you need it. It does want a proper outing every single day, though, and it leaves golden hair absolutely everywhere.
chienNous.p_golden_a: Count on a good hour's walk a day, a swim whenever there's water, and a sturdy vacuum cleaner. Left alone all day, it gets miserable.
chienNous.p_refuge_d: No particular breed for you two: your dog is waiting in a shelter, and it will be the one choosing you. A mixed breed often has a character all its own, and a gratitude you can see in its eyes. You won't know everything about its past, but the volunteers know it well and can tell you whether it likes children, cats or the sofa.
chienNous.p_refuge_a: Go and see it several times before you decide, take it for walks, and ask the shelter everything they know. An adult that is already calm and house-trained is often easier than a puppy.
chienNous.p_corgi_d: Short on legs, not on brains. The corgi is a former herding dog: it's lively, clever, loves to play and trots after you everywhere. It makes everyone laugh, it knows it, and it has an opinion on everything, which it shares out loud.
chienNous.p_corgi_a: It needs a real walk every day and something to keep its mind busy, or it will find its own entertainment. And keep a brush handy: it sheds all year round.
chienNous.p_bouledogue_d: The king of the apartment. It doesn't need to run for hours: it prefers the sofa, your lap, and a nap pressed up against you. It's funny, just stubborn enough, and it snores louder than the two of you put together.
chienNous.p_bouledogue_a: It copes badly with heat and hard exercise, and its health calls for a good vet. Choose a serious breeder who pays attention to how well their dogs breathe.
chienNous.p_cavalier_d: A dog made for cuddles. It's gentle, easy to live with, and it adapts to your pace: a walk if the weather's nice, a series if it rains. It loves everybody and asks for just one thing, which is to be with you.
chienNous.p_cavalier_a: That is also its weak spot: it really struggles with long days alone. Ask the breeder about the parents' heart checks too, as that is the breed's health problem.
chienNous.p_aussie_d: The dog for couples who never sit still. It runs, it jumps, it learns a trick in ten minutes and asks for more. It's very attached to its humans, to the point of following you into the bathroom. With this dog, lazy Sundays on the sofa are over, and that's partly why you want one.
chienNous.p_aussie_a: It needs two hours of activity a day, and not just walking: play, training, a dog sport. A bored Australian shepherd will redecorate your home.
chienNous.p_teckel_d: A big personality in a small, very long body. The dachshund is brave, stubborn, devoted to its humans, and it decides for itself whether the order you just gave is worth following. It's happy in a small apartment, it loves burrowing under the duvet, and it lets the whole building know when someone rings the bell.
chienNous.p_teckel_a: Look after its back: no stairs all day long, no jumping off the sofa, and no extra pounds. As for training, you'll have to be more stubborn than it is.
chienNous.p_caniche_d: Forget the cliché: the poodle is one of the most intelligent dogs there is. It understands everything, loves learning and playing, and stays close to its humans without being clingy. On top of that it hardly sheds, which settles the sofa question.
chienNous.p_caniche_a: Its coat never stops growing: plan a trip to the groomer every six to eight weeks, or learn to use the clippers. It comes in several sizes, from toy to standard.
chienNous.p_shiba_d: A cat in a dog's body. The Shiba is clean, calm at home, independent, and it loves you in its own way: from a distance, but for real. It copes with being alone better than most dogs, hardly ever barks, and its fox-like face turns heads in the street.
chienNous.p_shiba_a: That independence comes at a price: recall is never guaranteed, so keep it on a lead outdoors. And twice a year it sheds its undercoat by the handful.
chienNous.p_husky_d: An athlete made for the great outdoors. The husky was bred to pull sleds for hours: it needs exercise, space and cool weather. It's playful, talkative (it doesn't bark, it howls and “talks”), and independent enough to go exploring the moment a door is left open.
chienNous.p_husky_a: One for very sporty couples with a well-fenced garden. In an apartment or a hot climate, it's unhappy.
chienNous.p_bernois_d: A big teddy bear of around ninety pounds, calm and very gentle. The Bernese loves quiet walks, children, and lying down on your feet. It doesn't need to run: it needs room, cool weather, and you.
chienNous.p_bernois_a: Everything comes in a large size with this one: the food bill, the hair, the car you need to carry it. And its life is short, often seven to ten years, which is worth knowing before you get attached.
chienNous.p_peluche_d: Your answers say it kindly: it's not the right time yet. Between the days when nobody is home, the trips, and a wish that isn't quite the same on both sides, a real dog would spend a lot of time waiting for you. A plush one won't hold it against you.
chienNous.p_peluche_a: That doesn't mean never. Look after a friend's dog for a weekend, or volunteer to walk the dogs at a shelter: you'll soon know whether the idea holds up.
